content.text:
Start at https://pgcbasketball.com and complete the following task.

I’m trying to choose the best basketball camp for my 12-year-old son for a future school break or summer, and I don’t want a one-page answer that only checks one brand. Please start with PGC Basketball because that’s already on my radar, but then broaden naturally into a real parent decision: use my location if it’s available, or the nearest major metro you can infer from the browser, and build a shortlist of exactly 10 age-appropriate basketball camp options that are realistically reachable for us, prioritizing day camps and drivable options first but including strong overnight camps if they look meaningfully better. Make sure at least 3 of the 10 options are PGC camps if age-eligible and reachable, and fill the rest with credible alternatives from other organizations. For each camp, verify from the official public page the location, dates or session window, age or grade fit for a 12-year-old, camp type, price if shown, and whether it looks more skills-focused, shooting-focused, or general development; if something is missing, mark it as not shown. Then compare public ratings or parent-review signals wherever they exist, using Google, Yelp, Facebook, or other public review pages, and keep the most useful evidence tabs open rather than closing everything after you check it. Also open maps for the strongest contenders so you can compare actual distance or drive time, and note any obvious parent-logistics issues like overnight-only format, limited dates, or registration pages that look sold out or unclear. At the end, give me one ranked top-5 recommendation list pulled from the 10 camps, explain which single camp is the best overall choice versus which one is the best close-to-home choice, and leave the final shortlist and the key camp, review, and map pages open so I can inspect them myself. Put all the options in a CryptoPad Document with detailed analysis and comparisons.

Rules:
- You may use search engines and open new tabs. When the task asks you to leave a page open, keep it open in its own tab and say in your final answer which page is in which tab.
- Do NOT use cached/archived copies of pages (e.g. web.archive.org); work from the live sites.
- If a site you need is blocked (bot check, login wall, error), first try to get through it — complete a bot check yourself, retry, or use another route to the same page. If it still cannot be reached, say so explicitly in your answer and do not fill in from memory what you could not read on the page.
- When the task is complete, give your final answer as plain text in your last message.

   - *Score: 9.8/10 | Format: 5 Days / 4 Nights (40+ hrs) | Focus: Basketball IQ, Playmaking & Leadership*
   - *Why:* The gold standard in basketball IQ, decision-making, and leadership. 12-year-olds are introduced to collegiate-level film study and mental habits that transform how they see the floor. Located just 25.3 miles (30 min drive) up I-280.

   - *Score: 9.5/10 | Format: 3-Hour Weekend Clinics & Multi-Day Day Camps | Focus: Shooting Tech & Guard Skills*

What’s a Shooting College?

If you’ve ever watched your child pass up an open shot when you wanted nothing more than for them to have the confidence to take the shot, our Fall Weekend Shooting College can help.

And while we can’t magically make your child a great shooter in one weekend, we can give them the knowledge, skills and blueprint needed to quickly become a great shooter before the season starts.

The PGC Experience
What You'll Learn
10 Reasons to Register Today
Camp Details
FAQs
Your Child Deserves The Best Training – Period.

Sure, you can get world-class skills training in a few other places too.

But there’s no other place on the planet for players to develop their basketball IQ, mindset, leadership, playmaking, and confidence – all at the same time.

Here’s Why Your Child Needs to Develop These Skills »

Is PGC Shooting College Right For You?

Every fall, over 2,700 players from elementary school to high school attend a PGC Shooting College — but PGC is not for every player.

PGC is only for dedicated players who are serious about becoming better shooters.

Your child doesn’t have to take themselves too seriously in order to benefit from our camps (we still have lots of fun!), but they will need to enjoy working
=== PGC 2: Atherton Playmaker College ===

PLAYMAKER COLLEGE

Do You Want to Truly Help Your Child in Basketball?

None of us want our kids to get cut, sit on the bench, or fall short of their potential.

That’s painful to watch and it breaks our heart as parents.

That’s why we created the Playmaker College camp, so your child will finally get the roadmap, teachings, inspiration, and tools to make teams, get minutes, & stand out on the floor.

=== PGC 3: Belmont Point Guard Prep ===
REGISTER

Where Young Players Come to Discover HOW to Play the Game

Most day camps do a few drills and then roll out the balls for the kids to play. The camps are often fun, but lead to little lasting improvement.

At Point Guard Prep camps, players actually get better (while having lots of fun) as they discover the skills, habits, and winning mindset needed to make plays, score baskets, and lead their team.

The PGC Experience
What You’ll Get

Pricing

Your Child Deserves the Best Training — Period.

Typical camps with traditional ‘stations’ won’t help your child get ahead of the pack. Neither will just playing countless AAU games.

Young players need cutting-edge skill development, decision-making training, and loads of inspiration.

At a Point Guard Prep camp, players get all three.

Is PGC Right For Your Child?

Point Guard Prep camps are for incoming 4th-8th grade players — regardless of skill level, position or experience. However, if your child’s an experienced incoming 8th grade player, we recommend starting at our Playmaker College.

As long as your child wants to get better, they’ll have a fun and rewarding time with us. Want to make sure of it?

At Bay United, we believe in more than just wins—we believe in building great athletes and even better people. Through high-quality coaching, competitive play, and intentional development, your child will grow on and off the court.

Train with Purpose
1 weekday team practice + 1 optional skills session each week.
Compete with the Best
10 weekly games vs. top Bay Area talent (local travel), plus 2 weekend tournaments.
No Fear of Failure
We offer 3 levels of commitment, ensuring each athlete is challenged and supported.

More Than a Game: Over 100,000 kids participate in Legarza programs each year—and Bay United brings together the very best at every level. We place the child ahead of the player, and the player ahead of the team. Sports are a powerful tool for learning life lessons—and we’re here to help your child succeed long after the final buzzer. We will find the perfect spot for your athlete, register here to try out.

We’re building both boys and girls teams—Girls teams will be formed based on interest—the more who show up, the more we can offer. Encourage your daughter (and her friends!) to attend tryouts and help grow the future of Bay United girls basketball.

1 team practice/week + optional skills session, 10 games, 2 tournaments.

Practices will be held close to home—right in or near the neighborhoods where our players live. Games and tournaments will take place across the Bay Area, giving athletes the chance to compete against top teams from different regions.
